'''Mark Benecke''' (born 26 August 1970)<ref>{{Cite web|last=Benecke|first=Mark|date=7 October 2019|title=2005-08 Mark Benecke: Biography, CV & Who Is Who Entries|url=https://wiki2.benecke.com/index.php?title=2005-08_Mark_Benecke:_Biography,_CV_%26_Who_Is_Who_Entries}}</ref> is a German [[forensic biologist]].

== Career ==

=== Science ===
Benecke has worked on the identification of [[Adolf Hitler]] and [[Eva Braun]]'s dental remains in Moscow (as well as a skull fragment claimed to be Hitler's).<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130604094849/http://www.butlerfilms.tv/Work/C7698838-E8CD-429E-8D83-2D34BA814C26.html Hitler research in Moscow|"Hitler’s Skull -Riddles of the Dead"] (2003). [[National Geographic]].</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://braveplanetfilms.com/finding-hitlers-skull |title=Finding Hitler's Skull |last=Hoggard |first=Steve |date=2017 |publisher=Brave Planet Films |access-date=11 January 2021 |quote=In Hitler's Skull, forensic scientist Mark Benecke investigates the death of Adolf Hitler and takes viewers from the Holocaust Museum in Washington, D.C., to Lausanne Switzerland and into a Russian archive where fascinating evidence has been kept secret for almost half a century.}}</ref>{{efn|In 2009, [[DNA]] and forensic tests indicated that the skull belonged to a woman less than 40 years old.<ref>{{cite web | author = ABC News | title = DNA Test Sparks Controversy Over Hitler's Remains | website = ABC News | date = 9 December 2009 | url = https://abcnews.go.com/WN/hitler-skull-russian-secret-service-custody/story?id=9288287 | access-date = 15 February 2021}}</ref>}} He argued, in line with early investigator [[Hugh Trevor-Roper]] and scientific sources<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Castillo |first1=Rafael Fernández |last2=Ubelaker |first2=Douglas H. |last3=Acosta |first3=José Antonio Lorente |last4=Cañadas de la Fuente |first4=Guillermo A. |date=2013-03-10 |title=Effects of temperature on bone tissue. Histological study of the changes in the bone matrix |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0379073812005300 |journal=Forensic Science International |volume=226 |issue=1 |pages=33–37 |doi=10.1016/j.forsciint.2012.11.012 |hdl=10481/91826 |issn=0379-0738 |pmid=23287528 |hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Thompson |first1=Tim |last2=Gowland |first2=Rebecca |author-link2=Rebecca Gowland |title=What Happens to Human Bodies When They Are Burned? |url=https://www.futurelearn.com/info/courses/forensic-archaeology-and-anthropology/0/steps/67911 |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=[[Durham University]] |language=en-US |via=[[FutureLearn]]}}</ref> (including Hitler forensics expert [[Philippe Charlier]]),<ref>{{cite book |last1=Brisard |first1=Jean-Christophe |title=The Death of Hitler |last2=Parshina |first2=Lana |author-link2=Lana Parshina |publisher=[[Da Capo Press]] |year=2018 |isbn=978-0-306-92258-9 |pages=231 |language=en}}</ref> that [[body water]] would hinder an open-air cremation,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Benecke |first=Mark |date=2022-12-12 |orig-date=2003 |title=The Hunt for Hitler's Teeth |url=https://home.benecke.com/publications/the-hunt-for-hitlers-teeth |access-date=2024-03-04 |via=Dr. Mark Benecke |website=[[Bizarre (magazine)|Bizarre]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Trevor-Roper |first=Hugh |author-link=Hugh Trevor-Roper |url=https://archive.org/details/lastdaysofhitler0000trev_j2d4/ |title=The Last Days of Hitler |publisher=Pan Macmillan |year=2002 |isbn=978-0-330-49060-3 |edition=7th |location=London |pages=182 |orig-year=1947}}</ref> as opposed to American jurist [[Michael Musmanno]] (in 1950) and historians such as [[Anton Joachimsthaler]] (1995),<ref>{{cite book |last=Musmanno |first=Michael A. |author-link=Michael Musmanno |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_jNAAAAAIAAJ |title=Ten Days to Die |publisher=[[Doubleday (publisher)|Doubleday]] |year=1950 |location=Garden City, NY |language=en |pages=231–32, 234, 236, 238–39, 242–43}}</ref><ref name=anton>{{Cite book|last=Joachimsthaler|first=Anton|url=http://archive.org/details/lastdaysofhitler00joac|title=The Last Days of Hitler: The Legends, The Evidence, The Truth|publisher=[[Cassell (publisher)|Cassell]]|year=2000|isbn=978-1-85409-465-0|location=London|pages=166, 252–53|language=en|translator=Helmut Bölger|author-link=Anton Joachimsthaler|orig-year=1995}}</ref> who argued that a full cremation explains why nothing more than Hitler and Braun's dental remains were found.{{efn|Corpses [[The Death of Adolf Hitler|identified by the Soviets]] as Hitler and Braun's are widely disregarded<ref name=anton/> and considered by historian [[Mark Felton]] to evidence German fraud.<ref>{{cite episode |title=The Forgotten Theory |series=Find the Führer: The Secret Soviet Investigation |last=Felton |first=Mark |date=2023 |number=6}}</ref>}} The dental remains include part of the jawbone, intact (with superficial burning) but sundered at the [[alveolar process|depth of the teeth]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Bezymenski |first=Lev |url=https://archive.org/details/deathofadolfhitl0000unse_c0c9/page/44/mode/2up |title=The Death of Adolf Hitler |publisher=[[Harcourt, Brace & World]] |year=1968 |edition=1st |location=New York |page=45}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Charlier et al.|2018}}. "It is important to see that these data fit perfectly with the [Soviet] autopsy report and with our direct observations."</ref> According to Benecke, these either prove "that Hitler died in 1945 – or [[Conspiracy theories about Adolf Hitler's death|lived&nbsp;the rest of his life]] in Argentina without <nowiki>[</nowiki>[[mandibulectomy|part of his jaw]]]".<ref>{{Cite book |last=Benecke |first=Mark |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388722819_HITLER'S_SKULL_TEETH_A_STUDY_IN_3_LANGUAGES_ENGLISH_SPANISH_CHINESE |title=Hitler’s Skull and Teeth |date=2025 |publisher=Eygennutz Verlag |location=Hamm |pages=38}}</ref>

Benecke is the only forensic scientist to work on the case of Colombian serial killer and rapist [[Luis Garavito]].<ref>[https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/12462935 ''Luis Alfredo Garavito Cubillos: criminal and legal aspects of serial homicide with over 200 victims''], Arch Kriminol (2002) 210(3-4):83-94; [https://benecke.com/pdf/serial_killer_bartsch_mark_benecke.pdf pdf] of English language version</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/inside-mind-worlds-worst-serial-22290578 |title=Inside mind of 'world's worst serial killer' dubbed 'The Beast' who butchered 400 kids |last=Kitching |first=Chris |date=10 August 2020 |website=mirror.co.uk |access-date=11 January 2021|quote=Locked away after being sentenced to a record 1,853 years behind bars in Colombia, the psychopath readily described his vile crimes in gory detail to Dr Mark Benecke, the only forensic scientist he has ever agreed to speak to.}}</ref> Some of Benecke's forensic cases have been covered by the [[National Geographic Channel]] and the [[History (U.S. TV channel)|History Channel]].

Benecke has published several best-selling popular science books about the biology of aging, criminal cases and forensic biology.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.buchreport.de/?s=Mark+Benecke |title=Bestseller list|website=buchreport.de |publisher=[[Der Spiegel|Der SPIEGEL]] |access-date=11 January 2021}}</ref> He is a member of the editorial board of the ''[[Annals of Improbable Research]]'' (Cambridge, US), guest editor for ''[[Forensic Science International]]'' ([[Forensic Entomology]] Special Issue)<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20190217080932/http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/044e/31ac421c0ff706ab9f329ea5e1c6e4f89d98.pdf Example article "History of forensic entomology" from Forensic Science International special issue], republished in ''Acta Biologica Benrodis'' 14 (2008): 15-38</ref> and scientific advisor to the German [[scientific skepticism|skeptic]] organization [[Gesellschaft zur wissenschaftlichen Untersuchung von Parawissenschaften|GWUP]],<ref>[https://blog.gwup.net/tag/dr-mark-benecke/ Mark Benecke at GWUP]</ref> where he publishes skeptical articles on various topics, including his attempt to explain alleged signs of [[vampirism]].<ref>[https://roterdrache.org/catalog/English-Titles/Vampyres-among-us-Volume-III-ENGLISH::138.html ''Vampires among us, Volume III – A scientific study into vampyre identity groups and subcultures.''] (2015) {{ISBN|978-3939459958}}</ref> In 2001, Benecke was editor of the [[Forensic Science International]] special issue on forensic entomology.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/forensic-science-international/vol/120/issue/1
 |title=Volume 120, Issues 1–2, Pages 1-164 (15 August 2001) |editor-last=Benecke |editor-first=Mark  |date=15 August 2001 |website=Forensic Science International |publisher=Elsevier |access-date=11 January 2021}}</ref> In 2004, he was the guest editor of ''[[Anil Aggrawal's Internet Journal of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology]]'' for the [[Forensic entomology|Forensic Entomology]] Special Issue).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://benecke.com/pdf/forensic_entomology_special_issue_benecke_wells_goff_klotzbach_wolff_klotzbach_carvalho_turchetto_oliva_campobasso.pdf|title=Special Forensic Entomology Issue in Aggrawals's Journal}}</ref>

=== Other ventures ===
[[File:Mark Benecke Köln 2015.jpg|thumb|Benecke at a [[Die PARTEI]] event in 2015]]
In 2011, Benecke featured as a vocalist on [[Sara Noxx]]'s cover of [[Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds]]' song "[[Where the Wild Roses Grow]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.musicnonstop.co.uk/product-view.php?productid%3D24235 |title=Sara Noxx/Mark Benecke – Where the Wild Roses Grow |access-date=4 May 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720165612/http://www.musicnonstop.co.uk/product-view.php?productid=24235 |archive-date=20 July 2011}}</ref> In 2020, together with Bianca Stücker, he published a [[Leonard Cohen]] tribute cover album.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtl.de/cms/dr-mark-benecke-und-duettpartnerin-dr-bianca-stuecker-ueber-ihr-neues-album-we-want-it-darker-4621923.html |title="We want it darker" – eine Hommage an Leonard Cohen: Dr. Mark Benecke und Duett-Partnerin Dr. Bianca Stücker über ihr neues Album |access-date=11 January 2011|date=6 October 2020|first=Denise|last=Kylla|website=[[RTL (German TV channel)|RTL]]}}</ref>

Using the pseudonym "Belcanto Bene", Benecke was a member of the German punk band Die Blonden Burschen between 1989 and 2000.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fehling |title=Fehling und Benecke waren mit Bock die Blonden Burschen |trans-title=Fehling and Benecke were 'Die Blonden Burschen' ("The Blond Boys"), with passion |url=http://blog.luftschiff.org/notizen/2016/12/25/fehling-und-benecke-waren-mit-bock-die-blonden-burschen/ |website=Luftschiff |language=de |date=25 December 2016}}</ref>

In 2010, Benecke was candidate for the office of prime minister for Germany's largest state, [[North Rhine-Westphalia]], for the satirical political party [[Die PARTEI]]. Since 2010, he is chairman of Die PARTEI in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia.

== Personal life ==
Benecke was born in [[Rosenheim]], [[Bavaria]]. After receiving a [[List of doctoral degrees awarded by country#Germany|Dr. rer. medic.]] at [[Cologne]] University in 1997,<ref>Print of the Ph.D certificate in: Lachende Wissenschaft. Aus den Geheimarchiven des Spaß-Nobelpreises'', Lübbe, Bergisch-Gladbach 2005. {{ISBN|3-404-60556-X}} (German)]''</ref> he worked in the Chief Medical Examiner's Office in [[Manhattan]], New York, from 1997 to 1999. {{As of|1999}}, he works internationally on forensic cases as a freelance [[expert witness]]. He also teaches at various police academies and acts as a visiting professor to universities in Germany, England, Vietnam, Colombia, and the Philippines. He was married to the criminal psychologist [[Lydia Benecke]].
